accepted.justification: The exact images have no fstab entries. Declared execution is UID1000, read-only root, CapEff=0 and NoNewPrivs=1; no privileged mount caller or product mount endpoint exists. This excludes the required privileged fstab mount, not the presence of the installed util-linux package.

No fstab X-mount configuration exists; product processes do not invoke mount helpers. UID1000 with all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges cannot gain the privileged post-hook authority. Re-evaluate if privileged mounts or fstab entries are added.

No product or startup command invokes nsenter. The deployment uses a private PID namespace, no host cgroup mount and UID1000 with no capabilities; a privileged host operator running nsenter is outside this container workflow. The required root-created descriptor is absent.

The inspected fstab is empty and read-only; no X-mount.subdir operation is supplied by the product. UID1000/CapEff0/NoNewPrivs1 prohibit the privileged mount operation. Kernel version alone is not used to dismiss this CVE.

No fstab bind-mount authorization or X-mount hooks exist in the inspected runtime. Product subprocesses are fixed Python/LibreOffice/PostgreSQL tools, never mount; all capabilities are dropped and privilege gains disabled.

No product command invokes the gzip CLI; supported uploads are PNG/JPEG/CSV/XLSX, not LZW/LZH. HTTP compression and OOXML ZIP processing use distinct libraries, not the vulnerable sequential CLI decoder.

No privileged process runs in the declared API/web runtime. Node and product code do not call libacl pathname APIs; private artifact paths are generated by the server. UID1000, read-only root and CapEff0 exclude the required privileged ACL caller.

No product process invokes Perl or accepts a Perl regular-expression program. Web/API matching is JavaScript/Zod; renderer matching is Python. Actual web process tree/maps contain Node/Next only. The installed Perl CLI is not an input path.
An actual require Archive::Tar fails in both final images: the optional module is absent. Neither the web/API input contract nor the renderer calls Perl tar extraction.
The exact images are amd64 and Perl reports ivsize=8 and ptrsize=8; the upstream flaw is specific to a 32-bit Perl build.
An actual require Archive::Tar fails in both final images: the optional module is absent. Neither the web/API input contract nor the renderer calls Perl tar extraction.
Actual require probes show IO::Compress and File::GlobMapper absent. Product code has no Perl/glob evaluation endpoint; filenames are generated rather than executed.
No API, web, renderer or startup command invokes Perl pack/unpack. Uploaded data is decoded by the bounded Python readers and is not converted into Perl programs or templates.
Actual require Storable fails in both final images. Product persistence is PostgreSQL/JSON and no Storable input or Perl deserialization path is exposed.
